Dr Dodge - Fake Gynae

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A fake Gynae that was struck off the roll, is back in Cape Town operating under another name and destroying lives.

Unique Selling Point:
In 2013 Carte Blanche exposed Dr Ganesh Anil Anirudhra, a GP who was illegally practicing as a gynaecologist in Cape Town. At the time he was out on R20 000 bail after being charged with 319 counts of fraud in connection with defrauding medical schemes, as well as he Department of Labour Compensation Fund. He was subsequently struck off the roll by the HPCSA. He then went to work in the UK as a medical officer, moving to 4 different hospitals in 3 years. We will try and make enquiries about his performance record with those hospitals. He has since reinvented himself as Dr Anil Ramdhin, and is back practicing as a gynaecologist in Khayalitsha. Although he holds a Masters of Medicine in Obstetrics & Gynaecology from Medunsa - this was only awarded to him in 2019 after he took the University to court, claiming that they wouldn't give him the degree in 2010 due to racial discrimination. However, technically this does not make him a qualified Gynae. Nevertheless, he has been registered as a gynaecologist with the HPCSA since 2019. There is evidence he has used 12 different practice numbers.

Summary:
In April this year, Khayalitsha resident Zoleka Helesi (48) consulted Dr Ramdhin at the Khayalitsha Clinic. An ultrasound revealed she had Stage 4 cervical cancer. Dr Ramdhin admitted her to the Rondebosch Medical Centre in May where he an MRI revealed the true size of the cancerous mass in her cervix. She should have been referred to a specialist gynaecological oncologist for radiation etc,, instead Dr Ramdhin performed a total hysterectomy. The wound became severely septic. Surgeon Dr Bradley David then took over her case management and performed 4 follow-up operations to deal with gangrene and necrosis in her abdomen. All of this meant that radiation therapy was delayed by many critical months, and Zoleka is now hardly able to walk, needs a colostomy bag and her prognosis is very poor.

Further information:
Zoleka is an actress/director employed by the Baxter Theatre. She is unwilling to use her real name on TV but will give us an interview. Her boss, CEO Lara Foot has taken the issue further with the HPCSA, Rondebosch Medical Centre and Discovery Medical Aid. She wants Dr Ramdhin to pay for Zoleka's oncology treatment. She will explain their lack of response so far, and what the loss of Zoleka means to the Baxter.

Dr Caro Nel is gynaecologist who sold her thriving practice at Constantiaberg Mediclinic, and now lectures in O&G at UCT. She was a classmate of Dr Ganesh Anirudhra in 1997 when they were both specialising in O&G. She describes him as "completely unplayable", never contributing to the work and always sexually harassing nurses and female patients. He was eventually thrown out of the course. Dr Nel has positively identified Dr Ramdhin as the disgraced Dr Anirudhra. She is passionate about women's health and is outraged the he has been let loose on vulnerable women in Cape Town. She is adamant that she wants to confront him on camera about his fake ID and malpractice.

Flights to Cape Town

Script:


DR DODGE


V/O: In 2013 Carte Blanche exposed Cape Town doctor, Anil Anirudhra. Registered only as a GP, he was misrepresenting himself as a gynaecologist. He allegedly misdiagnosed conditions, misread ultrasounds and a hidden camera caught him making sexual innuendos while examining a patient.

Anirudhra: Have you ever had an Indian guy?

Patient: No!

V/O: He was facing 319 counts of medical aid fraud and had been arrested by the Hawks. He’d been convicted of fraud in 1992, and suspended from the South African Medical Register three times. After working in the UK for a few years, Dr Anirudhra was found guilty of serious professional misconduct in 2006, and struck off the Register. But in 2007 the HPCSA allowed him to re-register in South Africa on probation.

John: But are you a gynaecologist?

Anirudhra: I’m not registered as one at the moment.

John: Why does it say gynaecologist on your door?

Anirudhra: Silence

V/O: Eventually, he beat a hasty retreat.

After our broadcast the HPCSA took action against him in 2014, according to the current Acting-Registrar, Dr Munyadziwa Kwinda.

Kwinda: He was found guilty of unprofessional conduct based on those charges, practicing as a gynaecologist, and they imposed a penalty of a fine of R15 000.

V/O: The fraud charges were provisionally withdrawn in 2014, but Bonitas Medical Aid confirms the criminal investigation is ongoing.
Dr Anirudhra then legally changed his name to Anil Ramdhin and started practising as a GP in Khayelitsha.
In 2009 Medunsa had failed his MMed dissertation in gynaecology, but he took them to court. Ten years later, the Pretoria High Court ordered the University to award the M.Med degree, and in 2019 he officially registered as a gynaecologist. But the problems continue.

Nandi: Now I’m weak, you know. I just walk a little distance and I’m having short breath.

V/O: We found 48-year-old Nandi, at home in Khayelitsha, too weak to get out of bed. This award-winning actress and director from Cape Town’s Baxter Theatre asked us not to use her real name.

Nandi: In April I had to see the doctor because I was feeling some pain, abdominal pain. So I went to Doctor Ramdhin , and the doctor suspected that I've got fibroids.

Link: This is the Khayelitsha Medical Centre where Dr Ramdhin calls himself the Chief Medical Officer. It’s privately owned and from the outside it looks perfectly legitimate, and that is why Nandi chose this as her first port of call, even though as a medical aid patient she could have gone anywhere.

V/O Dr Ramdhin booked her into a small operating theatre a few kilometres away, where he performed a laparoscopy. He diagnosed cervical cancer.

Mac: Did he say you must see an oncologist, or suggest anything else?

Nandi: He didn’t suggest anything other than scaring me and saying that cancer is going to eat me out.

Johannes: In most cases what you would do is you would call a gynaecological oncologist to guide you and help you with the staging of this, and this is certainly not something that would fall within the scope of practice of a general gynaecologist to treat on his own.

V/O: Dr Johannes van Waart is the ex-officio President of SASOG, the South African Society for Obstetricians and Gynaecologists. We asked him what the prognosis for Stage 2 cervical cancer would be?

Johannes: If it is properly treated and a grade 2 cervical cancer, I think the prognosis is excellent, and I think the chance of that patient living to the end of their life is very, very good.

V/O: Instead, Dr Ramdhin recommended a total hysterectomy and booked Nandi into the Rondebosch Medical Centre where he also has rooms. On the 18th of May she had an MRI scan which revealed a large mass on her cervix. We showed the MRI report to retired gynaecologist Dr Caro Nel who now lectures student doctors at UCT.

Caro: The report mentions that there is a growth on the cervix measuring 55 millimetres, which is a very important finding because a tumour larger than four centimetres would possibly mean that there’s extension of this tumour elsewhere in the pelvis.

Mac: So would that mean you need to operate?

Caro: No, absolutely not, absolutely not. You would end cutting through the tumour, rather than getting 1cm clear margins around the tumour. So if you can’t do surgery, then combined chemotherapy radiotherapy is the treatment of choice. And one must remember that it’s not a second best treatment. It is the treatment.

V/O: But Dr Ramdhin chose to operate, and Nandi had a total hysterectomy. As next-of-kin she named her friend and boss, Baxter CEO Lara Foot.

Lara: This Doctor Ramdhin called me the next day after the operation, said that the operation was complete. And I said to him, OK, when will she be coming home? When do I need to collect her? And he said, no, no, it might be a while. It might be a week or two. I said, oh, OK. I said, did you get all the cancer out? And he said he wasn't sure, he wasn't sure, the thinks he did. Then a couple of days later I spoke to her on the telephone and she said that they’ve moved her to another ward because she was smelling so bad.

Nandi: I heard the doctors talking, saying this is a mess. Saying this is a mess, there was pus. And the nurses were calling the doctor and the doctor was nowhere to be found.

V/O: A week later Dr Ramdhin finally called in a general surgeon who performed an emergency procedure. Her wound was severely septic, with gangrene and necrosis of the skin. Nandi was in ICU for several weeks and underwent another 7 procedures before she could finally be discharged.

Lara: And so she stayed for months in the hospital. And all this time she was supposed to be having chemotherapy.

V/O: Four months after her cancer diagnosis Nandi eventually had chemo-radiation therapy, but the cancer had already spread.

Caro: Surgery is very risky. It could end up with a higher risk of fistula. A fistula is a connection or a hole between the bladder and the vagina, or between the rectum and the vagina, which would then lead to faeces and urine draining through the vagina.

V/O: This is precisely what happened to Nandi.

Nandi: When I went to hospital I was in high heels. I was driving. I was fresh. But when I came out of hospital it was something that’s ended up to this.

Lara: Besides the trauma of all these operations, the indignity of what has now happened to her insides which are in a shambles, she’s left with very little hope because the chemo is not working.

Mac link: We came looking for Dr Ramdhin at his rooms at the Rondebosch Medical Centre, but he’s not available today. According to his receptionist he has 12 surgeries booked and will be in theatre all day.

V/O: As next-of-kin Lara has not agreed to release Dr Ramdhin from doctor/patient confidentiality to discuss Nandi’s case with Carte Blanche. But he claims we are trying to attribute blame for a pre-existing condition, and he cannot respond as the matter is before the HPCSA.

V/O Last year Lara laid a formal complaint with the HPCSA about Dr Ramdhin’s treatment of Nandi.

Kwinda: With Nandi’s case, we are looking at possibly invoking our suspension regulations. Cases of negligence, where we realize that there is risk to patients, we invoke our suspension regulations.

Mac link: This is the Colleges of Medicine of South Africa, a custodian of the quality of medical care in our country. To practice as a specialist gynaecologist you have to pass their exams and become a Fellow of the College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, or FCOG..

V/O: According to the Khayelitsha Medical Centre’s website, Dr Ramdhin became a Fellow of the College in 1995. But they have no record of him. The website also falsely claims he’s been a Member of the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists since 2004. When asked to explain, Dr Ramdhin responded:

Text: This is a surprise as I certainly did not make any claim to this effect.

Kwinda: That is really misrepresentation, and it just shows lack of integrity.

V/O: In August last year, Beauty Mama was diagnosed with a suspected ovarian cyst at Port Elizabeth’s Dora Nginza Hospital. When no specialist was available to remove it, her 19-year-old daughter Zainab went online to find a gynaecologist.

Zainab: So I got ahold of this Dr Anil Ramdhin; and when I was reading his website - like anyone would, you would say wow, this is an amazing doctor 'cause of all the things that he claims to have achieved. And I contacted him and I told him my situation, my mom needs laparoscopic surgery. He’s like OK, no it's fine, I can assist you with that. So I asked him how much would it be for the surgery, like for the whole procedure? He’s like just give me 50,000 and everything can be sorted for your mom.

V/O: But they didn’t have 50 000, so they sold their house in Port Elizabeth.
On the 21st of August they consulted Dr Ramdhin at the Rondebosch Medical Centre.

Zainab: So he did an ultrasound, he's like no Mama, no - because you know the initial report said that the cyst is around 20 centimeters - so he was like no mama, you need to get surgery quick-quick because now this thing is around 40 to 50 centimeters now.

V/O; Their attorney deposited R50 000 into Dr Ramdhin’s account, and the next day they caught a cab to the operating theatre in Khayelitsha.

Zainab: He actually told me that day that since the mass is so huge a laparoscopic wouldn’t be, you know, good enough. What needed to be done was a open surgery.

V/O: Zainab watched her mother being wheeled into theatre for a midline laparotomy. Forty minutes later, Dr Ramdhin came out and spoke to her.

Zainab: We did the surgery on your mom but it doesn’t look good. I was like what do you mean it doesn’t look good? And he said that you know like it’s better that you see for yourself.

V/O: He then took her from the ward into the operating theatre.

Zainab: There was this big bowl in front of me like set on the table there - and inside this bowl is a lot of you know things in it; and my mom is just lying on the bed like on my left-hand side. She's laying there and she still, she's…

Mac: She was still open?

Zainab: She was still open and he showed me this big bowl, he's like this is what we took out of your mom, and he’s like inside it doesn't look good I have to tell you that your mom has cancer, and by the looks of it it's already stage four. He said all you have to do right now is just give your mother all the love and care because she's going to die soon. And then he said that I had to tell my Mom the news.

V/O: Three hours after the surgery, he discharged Beauty Mama. Within days her condition had worsened, so they sought help at Groote Schuur Hospital. But they required a referral letter, so Zainab called Dr Ramdhin.

Zainab: He said if you want a referral letter go to Khayelitsha, and I told him but Khayelitsha’s too far for us to go there, and we don't have our own car. He’s like then I don't know what you're going to do. Now stop bothering me, and then he dropped the call.

V/O; A private GP finally referred Beauty to New Somerset Hospital, where a gynae-oncologist told Zainab that Dr Ramdhin had botched the surgery.

Zainab: I honestly felt like dying, cos now my mom is in that situation because of a doctor I contacted.

V/O: Beauty returned to Port Elizabeth but spent her last weeks in hospital almost unable to recognize her daughter.

Zainab: Mama…..

V/O: She passed away less than a month after the surgery, at the age of 46.

Mac link: The case of Beauty Mama has also been reported to the HPCSA. Once again a cancer patient was allegedly subjected to unnecessary surgery, and her own daughter exposed to unacceptable trauma.

V/O: Dr Ramdhin wouldn’t answer any questions as he’s bound by doctor/patient confidentiality. When Zainab granted him permission, he didn’t respond. SASOG’s experts believe his treatment of both patients probably represents unprofessional conduct and practicing outside his scope of practice.

Zainab: I’d like to see him locked up for a very long time because right now, right here as I’m with you, talking to you, I don’t have my mom.

Nandi: He needs to stop this before it’s too late.

V/O: Two weeks after our interview, Nandi passed away in hospital with her sister and Lara by her side.

Lara: This Doctor Ramdhin called me the next day after the operation, said that the operation was complete. And I said to him, OK, when will she be coming home? When do I need to collect her? And he said, no, no, it might be a while. It might be a week or two. I said, oh, OK. I said, did you get all the cancer out? And he said he wasn't sure, he wasn't sure, the thinks he did. Then a couple of days later I spoke to her on the telephone and she said that they’ve moved her to another ward because she was smelling so bad. Nandi: I heard the doctors talking, saying this is a mess. Saying this is a mess, there was pus. And the nurses were calling the doctor and the doctor was nowhere to be found. V/O: A week later Dr Ramdhin finally called in a general surgeon who performed an emergency procedure. Her wound was severely septic, with gangrene and necrosis of the skin. Nandi was in ICU for several weeks and underwent another 7 procedures before she could finally be discharged. Lara: And so she stayed for months in the hospital. And all this time she was supposed to be having chemotherapy. V/O: Four months after her cancer diagnosis Nandi eventually had chemo-radiation therapy, but the cancer had already spread. Caro: Surgery is very risky. It could end up with a higher risk of fistula. A fistula is a connection or a hole between the bladder and the vagina, or between the rectum and the vagina, which would then lead to faeces and urine draining through the vagina. V/O: This is precisely what happened to Nandi. Nandi: When I went to hospital I was in high heels. I was driving. I was fresh. But when I came out of hospital it was something that’s ended up to this. Lara: Besides the trauma of all these operations, the indignity of what has now happened to her insides which are in a shambles, she’s left with very little hope because the chemo is not working. Mac link: We came looking for Dr Ramdhin at his rooms at the Rondebosch Medical Centre, but he’s not available today. According to his receptionist he has 12 surgeries booked and will be in theatre all day. V/O: As next-of-kin Lara has not agreed to release Dr Ramdhin from doctor/patient confidentiality to discuss Nandi’s case with Carte Blanche. But he claims we are trying to attribute blame for a pre-existing condition, and he cannot respond as the matter is before the HPCSA. V/O Last year Lara laid a formal complaint with the HPCSA about Dr Ramdhin’s treatment of Nandi. Kwinda: With Nandi’s case, we are looking at possibly invoking our suspension regulations. Cases of negligence, where we realize that there is risk to patients, we invoke our suspension regulations. Mac link: This is the Colleges of Medicine of South Africa, a custodian of the quality of medical care in our country. To practice as a specialist gynaecologist you have to pass their exams and become a Fellow of the College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, or FCOG.. V/O: According to the Khayelitsha Medical Centre’s website, Dr Ramdhin became a Fellow of the College in 1995. But they have no record of him. The website also falsely claims he’s been a Member of the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists since 2004. When asked to explain, Dr Ramdhin responded: Text: This is a surprise as I certainly did not make any claim to this effect. Kwinda: That is really misrepresentation, and it just shows lack of integrity. V/O: In August last year, Beauty Mama was diagnosed with a suspected ovarian cyst at Port Elizabeth’s Dora Nginza Hospital. When no specialist was available to remove it, her 19-year-old daughter Zainab went online to find a gynaecologist. Zainab: So I got ahold of this Dr Anil Ramdhin; and when I was reading his website - like anyone would, you would say wow, this is an amazing doctor 'cause of all the things that he claims to have achieved. And I contacted him and I told him my situation, my mom needs laparoscopic surgery. He’s like OK, no it's fine, I can assist you with that. So I asked him how much would it be for the surgery, like for the whole procedure? He’s like just give me 50,000 and everything can be sorted for your mom. V/O: But they didn’t have 50 000, so they sold their house in Port Elizabeth. On the 21st of August they consulted Dr Ramdhin at the Rondebosch Medical Centre. Zainab: So he did an ultrasound, he's like no Mama, no - because you know the initial report said that the cyst is around 20 centimeters - so he was like no mama, you need to get surgery quick-quick because now this thing is around 40 to 50 centimeters now. V/O; Their attorney deposited R50 000 into Dr Ramdhin’s account, and the next day they caught a cab to the operating theatre in Khayelitsha. Zainab: He actually told me that day that since the mass is so huge a laparoscopic wouldn’t be, you know, good enough. What needed to be done was a open surgery. V/O: Zainab watched her mother being wheeled into theatre for a midline laparotomy. Forty minutes later, Dr Ramdhin came out and spoke to her. Zainab: We did the surgery on your mom but it doesn’t look good. I was like what do you mean it doesn’t look good? And he said that you know like it’s better that you see for yourself. V/O: He then took her from the ward into the operating theatre. Zainab: There was this big bowl in front of me like set on the table there - and inside this bowl is a lot of you know things in it; and my mom is just lying on the bed like on my left-hand side. She's laying there and she still, she's… Mac: She was still open? Zainab: She was still open and he showed me this big bowl, he's like this is what we took out of your mom, and he’s like inside it doesn't look good I have to tell you that your mom has cancer, and by the looks of it it's already stage four. He said all you have to do right now is just give your mother all the love and care because she's going to die soon. And then he said that I had to tell my Mom the news. V/O: Three hours after the surgery, he discharged Beauty Mama. Within days her condition had worsened, so they sought help at Groote Schuur Hospital. But they required a referral letter, so Zainab called Dr Ramdhin. Zainab: He said if you want a referral letter go to Khayelitsha, and I told him but Khayelitsha’s too far for us to go there, and we don't have our own car. He’s like then I don't know what you're going to do. Now stop bothering me, and then he dropped the call. V/O; A private GP finally referred Beauty to New Somerset Hospital, where a gynae-oncologist told Zainab that Dr Ramdhin had botched the surgery. Zainab: I honestly felt like dying, cos now my mom is in that situation because of a doctor I contacted. V/O: Beauty returned to Port Elizabeth but spent her last weeks in hospital almost unable to recognize her daughter. Zainab: Mama….. V/O: She passed away less than a month after the surgery, at the age of 46. Mac link: The case of Beauty Mama has also been reported to the HPCSA. Once again a cancer patient was allegedly subjected to unnecessary surgery, and her own daughter exposed to unacceptable trauma. V/O: Dr Ramdhin wouldn’t answer any questions as he’s bound by doctor/patient confidentiality. When Zainab granted him permission, he didn’t respond. SASOG’s experts believe his treatment of both patients probably represents unprofessional conduct and practicing outside his scope of practice. Zainab: I’d like to see him locked up for a very long time because right now, right here as I’m with you, talking to you, I don’t have my mom. Nandi: He needs to stop this before it’s too late. V/O: Two weeks after our interview, Nandi passed away in hospital with her sister and Lara by her side. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A fake Gynae that was struck off the roll, is back in Cape Town operating under another name and destroying lives.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: In 2013 Carte Blanche exposed Dr Ganesh Anil Anirudhra, a GP who was illegally practicing as a gynaecologist in Cape Town. At the time he was out on R20 000 bail after being charged with 319 counts of fraud in connection with defrauding medical schemes, as well as he Department of Labour Compensation Fund. He was subsequently struck off the roll by the HPCSA. He then went to work in the UK as a medical officer, moving to 4 different hospitals in 3 years. We will try and make enquiries about his performance record with those hospitals. He has since reinvented himself as Dr Anil Ramdhin, and is back practicing as a gynaecologist in Khayalitsha. Although he holds a Masters of Medicine in Obstetrics & Gynaecology from Medunsa - this was only awarded to him in 2019 after he took the University to court, claiming that they wouldn't give him the degree in 2010 due to racial discrimination. However, technically this does not make him a qualified Gynae. Nevertheless, he has been registered as a gynaecologist with the HPCSA since 2019. There is evidence he has used 12 different practice numbers.
metadata.Summary: In April this year, Khayalitsha resident Zoleka Helesi (48) consulted Dr Ramdhin at the Khayalitsha Clinic. An ultrasound revealed she had Stage 4 cervical cancer. Dr Ramdhin admitted her to the Rondebosch Medical Centre in May where he an MRI revealed the true size of the cancerous mass in her cervix. She should have been referred to a specialist gynaecological oncologist for radiation etc,, instead Dr Ramdhin performed a total hysterectomy. The wound became severely septic. Surgeon Dr Bradley David then took over her case management and performed 4 follow-up operations to deal with gangrene and necrosis in her abdomen. All of this meant that radiation therapy was delayed by many critical months, and Zoleka is now hardly able to walk, needs a colostomy bag and her prognosis is very poor.
metadata.Further information: Zoleka is an actress/director employed by the Baxter Theatre. She is unwilling to use her real name on TV but will give us an interview. Her boss, CEO Lara Foot has taken the issue further with the HPCSA, Rondebosch Medical Centre and Discovery Medical Aid. She wants Dr Ramdhin to pay for Zoleka's oncology treatment. She will explain their lack of response so far, and what the loss of Zoleka means to the Baxter. Dr Caro Nel is gynaecologist who sold her thriving practice at Constantiaberg Mediclinic, and now lectures in O&G at UCT. She was a classmate of Dr Ganesh Anirudhra in 1997 when they were both specialising in O&G. She describes him as "completely unplayable", never contributing to the work and always sexually harassing nurses and female patients. He was eventually thrown out of the course. Dr Nel has positively identified Dr Ramdhin as the disgraced Dr Anirudhra. She is passionate about women's health and is outraged the he has been let loose on vulnerable women in Cape Town. She is adamant that she wants to confront him on camera about his fake ID and malpractice.
